title: Puck world projection (puck.world.projection.v1)
description: puck.world.projection.v1 — what an authority hands a peer holding the Presentation tier. A separate versioned document rather than a WorldDefinition with sections nulled out, because WorldDefinition requires 33 sections and a partial one either refuses at RequireSections or misreports what it carries. This type's member list is the disclosure decision: a section that must not leave an authority below the replica tier has no member here. Absent by construction: rules, grants, state, market, admission, generation, generators, groups, properties, addons, storage, host, authoring, identity, inputHold, targetRegisters, bodyMotionPrograms, portals, and every kit's producers/actions (see WorldProjectedKit). Adjacencies, Destinations, References, and Interactions cross because TryDeriveOverlap reads them from both sides of a seam and must derive the same depth on each; withholding one side's inputs desymmetrizes it silently. Metadata crosses in reduced form: WorldProjectedMetadata carries title/description only — a world's authored name and blurb are harmless to a presentation-tier peer. authors, tags, and custom never cross; custom in particular is an unbounded author scratch bag that may hold notes never meant to leave the authority.

provenance.description: Who composed this, from what, at which revision and tier.

authority.description: The composing authority's own addressable namespace (a host.authority endpoint, or the process-local boot namespace for an in-process authority).

documentId.description: The source document's stable id, when it carries one.

revision.description: The source document's revision at composition.

tier.description: The tier this projection was composed at — always Presentation today, since Replica sends the definition verbatim and Frames sends no document at all.

moveSpeed.description: Locomotion speed in world units per second — the profileless fallback a stand-in advances on (a seated player reads its live profile's speed instead, so identity.motion stays real-time).

turnSpeed.description: Turn speed in radians per second (the profileless fallback counterpart to MoveSpeed).

maxSmoothError.description: The largest server-correction position error, in world units, that presentation may ease instead of snapping.

items.description: One named spawn pose available to seats and population policies.

id.description: The stable spawn name, unique within the definition.

yawDegrees.description: The spawn yaw about +Y, in degrees.

shadowCrowdRadius.description: The boot soft-shadow crowd radius (world units).

upscaleSharpness.description: The boot reduced-resolution reconstruction blend (0 bilinear .. 1 Catmull-Rom).

shadows.description: The soft-shadow tier the preset selects.

ambientOcclusion.description: Whether the preset enables ambient occlusion.

renderScale.description: The render-scale tier the preset selects.

extensions.description: The post-render extension chain, composed over the world's rendered output in list order — e.g. [{ "id": "sdf-film-grain", "config": { "intensity": 0.08 } }]. Optional; an absent or empty list is the byte-identical default path (no extension composed). Every id must name a shipped shader set — a puck.shader.v1 manifest's file stem (checked at document load); each entry's own config is validated against that manifest's declared config schema at boot and by puck schema.

items.description: One entry in Extensions — a shipped shader set's id plus the values for its manifest-declared config fields.

id.description: The shader set id (its puck.shader.v1 manifest's file stem) — checked against the shipped vocabulary at document load (IsRegisteredPostRenderExtension), never interpreted here.

config.description: The set's config values, or null when the manifest declares none or every field has a default. Not validated at document load — the manifest's declared config schema validates it at boot (matching Machine's Options, the identical shallow-then-deep precedent), refusing boot with the set id and reason on a malformed value.
Film grain: a per-pixel integer-hashed offset added over the rendered output. The hash is a pure function of pixel cell, grain frame, and seed, so it renders identically on both backends.

size.description: The grain cell size, in pixels.

seed.description: Folded into the per-pixel hash; two worlds with different seeds grain differently.

flickerHz.description: How many times per second the grain pattern advances; the pattern is keyed on the simulation clock, so a frame carries the grain of the flicker period its tick falls in.

lighting.description: The scene's directional sun and ambient term. Optional, and every field within it is optional individually — an absent section, or an absent field within it, resolves to SdfFrame's pinned default for that field, so a world renders unchanged until it authors one.

direction.description: The direction from a lit surface toward the light, any nonzero length (normalized host-side before upload).

hemisphere.description: The hemisphere gradient, scaling surface normal Y.

sky.description: The procedural sky — a gradient, sun disc, star field, and distance fog. Optional; an absent section renders the pinned two-stop gradient and 0.015 fog density bit-exactly, as before this section existed.

zenith.description: The straight-up sky color, as #RRGGBB. Optional; absent takes the pinned zenith.

horizon.description: The horizon-band color (the gradient's middle stop), as #RRGGBB. Optional; absent takes the midpoint between the pinned ground and zenith.

ground.description: The straight-down (nadir) color, as #RRGGBB. Optional; absent takes the pinned ground.

fogDensity.description: The exponential distance-fog density fading toward the sky color. Optional; absent takes the pinned 0.015 — the exact value the fog term used before this field existed.

sun.description: The visible sun disc, drawn about the lighting sun's direction. Optional; absent draws no disc.

discRadians.description: The disc's angular half-radius in radians, in (0, π/2]. Controls the falloff sharpness: a smaller disc reads sharper.

stars.description: The procedural star field. Optional; absent draws no stars.

density.description: The star grid's cell count per octahedral axis. A higher value packs more, smaller stars.

seed.description: The hash seed folded into every cell — a different seed reshuffles the field.

twinkle.description: Scintillation for a share of the stars. Optional; absent twinkles none.

share.description: The fraction of stars that twinkle, in [0, 1]. Zero twinkles none.

depth.description: How far a twinkling star dips below its steady brightness, in [0, 1]: 0 holds steady, 1 dips to black.

rate.description: The fundamental scintillation rate in hertz; each star twinkles at a small harmonic of it.

clouds.description: The procedural cloud layer. Optional; absent draws no clouds.

coverage.description: The fraction of the sky the layer covers, in [0, 1]. Zero draws none.

softness.description: The width of a cloud's edge, in (0, 1]: small is hard-edged cumulus, large is a diffuse haze.

scale.description: The size of one cloud cell in layer units (the layer sits at unit height, so a scale of 1 spans about 45° overhead). Larger is broader clouds.

seed.description: The hash seed folded into the lattice — a different seed reshapes the layer.

color.description: The cloud colour, as #RRGGBB or a state.<row>.<key> binding. Optional; absent is white.

drift.description: The layer's wind, in layer units per second along world X and Z, integrated on the tick clock. Optional; absent holds still.

spin.description: The layer's rotation about the zenith in radians per second — the planetary-scale turning a rotating frame gives a broad flow; positive is counter-clockwise seen from below. Optional; absent is none.

curl.description: The Coriolis twist: how far, in radians, the layer is wound about the zenith at 45° elevation, the winding falling off toward the horizon and the zenith so bands spiral in rather than shear apart. Positive winds counter-clockwise. Optional; absent is none.

shear.description: The wind of the SHAPING field relative to the cloud field, in layer units per second: the two slide past each other, so clouds boil and re-form as they drift rather than glide as a fixed picture. Optional; absent holds their shapes.

cycle.description: Lighting and sky keyed over a state row's value (a day/night cycle when that row advances). Optional; absent leaves Lighting/Sky static.

state.description: The state row read (its slot cell; Fixed or Int).

keys.description: At least two keys, strictly ascending At in [0, 1).

items.description: One point on a WorldRenderCycle.

at.description: The row-value fraction this key sits at, in [0, 1).

lighting.description: The lighting fields this key moves, or null.

sky.description: The sky fields this key moves, or null.

zenith.description: The straight-up sky color, as #RRGGBB. Optional; absent takes the pinned zenith.

horizon.description: The horizon-band color (the gradient's middle stop), as #RRGGBB. Optional; absent takes the midpoint between the pinned ground and zenith.

ground.description: The straight-down (nadir) color, as #RRGGBB. Optional; absent takes the pinned ground.

fogDensity.description: The exponential distance-fog density fading toward the sky color. Optional; absent takes the pinned 0.015 — the exact value the fog term used before this field existed.

items.description: One diegetic screen in the world — a screen slab emitted by SdfProgramBuilder whose lit face samples a bound source (or the procedural fallback when unbound). The frame (Origin/Right/ Up + HalfWidth/HalfHeight) is the sampled surface frame and must match the slab's placement; the frame source bakes the geometry translate from it.

index.description: The engine screen-surface index (0..MaxScreenSurfaces−1) this slab declares — the key the source/light providers bind under.

origin.description: The front face's world-space center (the sampled surface origin); the geometry center sits one HalfDepth behind it along the face normal.

right.description: The unit world axis the sampled U increases along (the slab's local +X in world space).

up.description: The unit world axis the sampled V increases against — V = 0 at the top (the slab's local +Y in world space).

halfWidth.description: The face half-width (the slab's local X half-extent).

halfHeight.description: The face half-height (the slab's local Y half-extent).

halfDepth.description: The slab's local Z half-extent (its thickness behind the face).

source.description: The signal the lit face carries.

anyOf.description: No provider is bound — the engine lights the slot with its procedural no-signal fallback (an animated test-card / striped no-signal look, never black).
The deterministic animated test pattern (Puck.SdfVm.Views.TestPatternSource), rendered from the world's sim tick (never the wall clock) into a CPU buffer and uploaded each frame.

width.description: The pattern framebuffer width in pixels.

height.description: The pattern framebuffer height in pixels.

anyOf.description: An arbitrary deterministic machine's unresampled framebuffer — resolved against a registered IScreenMachineEngine by Engine id. The world never names a concrete machine: the engine owns its Options vocabulary (a GamingBrick reads a dmg/cgb/agb model + a dmgspeed pin).

contentPath.description: The content file (a cartridge ROM) the machine boots, or empty when the screen is unconfigured — the binder faults the slot gracefully (no crash, no-signal card) rather than booting.

options.description: The engine-specific options string, or null for the engine's defaults.

anyOf.description: The platform's default live camera feed, with an explicit preferred capture profile. The platform may negotiate a nearby extent; every screen sampling the same physical default device shares one session.

profile.description: The preferred capture extent and maximum upload cadence.

refreshRateHz.description: Maximum pull/upload cadence; it must divide the engine time base exactly.

anyOf.description: A named view from the presentation view stack, such as a monitor showing another camera's output.

cameraName.description: The registered view name this slot samples.

anyOf.description: A live compositor capture feed — a desktop window keyed by title, or a whole monitor keyed by index. The selector is the altitude of the primitive: MonitorIndex null is window mode; non-null is whole-monitor mode (and WindowTitle is unused).

windowTitle.description: The captured window's title (window mode; ignored when MonitorIndex is set).

profile.description: This capture consumer's output extent and maximum refresh cadence.

refreshRateHz.description: Maximum pull/upload cadence; it must divide the engine time base exactly.

monitorIndex.description: The 0-based monitor to capture whole (0 = primary), or null for window mode.

anyOf.description: A screen showing the developer console as an object in the world — the diegetic half of the control plane the unification contract names ("the on-screen panel and process stdin"). The frame is CPU-composed into a CRT-styled framebuffer and pushed through IGpuSurfaceUpload, exactly as the ported console feed does; nothing about it is a render-graph node. Complementary to — never a duplicate of — ConsoleTape, which publishes the same content to the screen-space overlay. At most one console source may be live (declared) at a time; an unselected console entry sitting in a magazine is legal.

rows.description: Console text rows the framebuffer composes, 1..120. Sizes the CPU buffer.

procedural.description: When true the slot shows the sibling generated pattern instead of console text — carried as a mode of this variant rather than as a seventh union case.

anyOf.description: An authorable QR code (ISO/IEC 18004) — the document names a payload string and the engine derives the scannable module grid (QrEncoder), rendered CPU-side into a static B8G8R8A8 framebuffer and uploaded once, never re-derived from the tick like TestPattern. The driving case is a link one human hands another off an in-world screen. This record is the document-authored half only — nothing here mints a payload at runtime; screen.source <index> qr is the live-authoring twin, and world.identify is the one caller that mints its payload (the running world's own documentId and content-address pin) rather than being handed one.

payload.description: The encoded string, UTF-8 byte mode. Must fit within version MaxSupportedVersion at EcLevel — validation refuses an oversized payload by name (its byte count against the level's capacity), never truncates it.

ecLevel.description: The error-correction level: L, M, Q, or H (case-insensitive, parsed by TryParse). Defaults to M.

quietZoneModules.description: The white quiet-zone border width in modules on every side. ISO/IEC 18004 recommends at least 4; a smaller value authors a QR a real scanner may refuse to read (a borderless QR does not scan) — the document may still author it (validation only refuses a negative width), since a screen's physical framing sometimes supplies the margin itself.

anyOf.description: A live rendered view of another world, resolved through a destinations row (docs/vision.md, "Observation and display"). The face/screen resolves the same resolver-owned identity a portal crossing at the same door would land in (WorldSessionResolver), attaches an observation lease to the resolved instance's server, and mirrors just enough of its delivered definition/snapshots to render its static authored geometry through CameraName (or the destination's default projection). It never re-derives durability/scope/generation itself — those are the destination row's own facts.

destination.description: The Name this face/screen observes. Must resolve to a declared destinations row — an undeclared name refuses at boot (validated, like a portal facet's own destination).

camera.description: The destination's own placeable-camera name to render through, or null for its default projection (its first declared camera, else a fixed overview derived from its spawn points). Wire name camera — plain Camera would collide with the sibling Camera arm's own type name inside this enclosing record. Validated only as non-empty when present at author time — the destination's own definition is not joined at boot (references assert naming intent, not reachability), so an unknown camera name is refused loudly at bind time instead, once the destination is actually resolved, falling back to the default projection rather than refusing the whole bind. Ignored under Window (see Projection).

projection.description: How the destination render projects onto this face (see WorldScreenProjection). Default Camera — unauthored worlds and every session facet authored before this member existed render byte-identically. Optional and trailing (the same widen-without-moving-existing-members shape CameraName itself already follows). Window requires this same face's Portal to author Mapped with a Counterpart — refused by name otherwise (see WorldDefinitionValidator); a top-level screens row or magazine entry carries no face to pair with, so window is refused there unconditionally.

resolution.description: The offscreen target's [width, height] in pixels, or null for the engine default (Puck.SdfVm.Views.WorldSessionView.DefaultWidth x DefaultHeight — today's 160x144 panel, unchanged for an unauthored facet). Each axis is validated within 1..WorldDefinitionValidator.MaxSurfaceDimension. Omitted from the wire when null.

anyOf.description: Authored reading text on the screen face, rendered through the engine's glyph-decal tier (Puck.SdfVm.SdfWorldEngine.SetScreenDecal): a fixed monospace cell grid sampled from the world's packed font atlas at shade time — the dense-text sibling of a creation's textRuns, which stamp marched Glyph geometry. Signs, plaques, books, and monitors author this; short sculptural lettering stays a text run. Requires the world to declare a text font catalog (Text); the decal bypasses the CRT image pipeline, so no image source competes with it on the slot.

lines.description: The text rows, top-down; each row maps onto one grid row of cells (row-major, one scalar per cell — no kerning or shaping on this tier).

font.description: The text catalog font name; null selects the catalog's default font.

columns.description: The cell grid's column count, or null to fit the widest line. The grid (columns x rows) is capped by the engine's per-screen decal cell budget (Puck.SignedDistance.SdfScreenDecalLayout.MaxScreenDecalCells).

rows.description: The cell grid's row count, or null to fit the line count.

foreground.description: The letter color as #RRGGBB, or null for white.

background.description: The cell background color as #RRGGBB, or null for black.

engageable.description: Whether a player may engage this screen.

engageRadius.description: The world-unit radius a player must be inside to engage (meaningful only when Engageable). Validated finite and non-negative.

autoInsert.description: When set, engaging the screen first boots the selected magazine entry (the "walk over, press the button, the screen lights" gesture), so the interaction is one act rather than an insert then an engage.

engageChannel.description: The world-event channel whose arrival on a body engages this screen, or null (the default) for a route that does not answer gestures. The author chooses this name freely; the engine never special-cases a spelling. Omitted from the wire when null.

cycleChannel.description: Same, for advancing the magazine selector. Omitted from the wire when null.

channels.description: The declared channel names this route's mask reaches — a masked-out channel keeps flowing to the routed body's own pose (relevant under the capture:false mirror policy) but never reaches this route's target. null (the default) reaches every declared channel. Omitted from the wire when null.

translation.description: The authored channel→pad-element rows this route's target reads, replacing the engine's default when present. null uses the engine mapping. Omitted from the wire when null.

items.description: One authored channel→pad-element mapping row — a Translation entry.

channel.description: The declared channel name this row reads.

element.description: The neutral pad element the channel's value drives.

solid.description: The screen slab's solidity facet (a box collider derived from the slab's oriented frame + Margin by Server.WorldColliderSet), or null for a decorative screen. Omitted from the wire when null.

margin.description: The signed skin added to the shape for contact purposes. Positive fattens the collider past the drawn surface; negative lets a body sink in. Compensates the smooth-union blend.

magazine.description: The per-screen source magazine (the cycle primitive), or null for a screen with no magazine — nothing to cycle. Omitted from the wire when null — the whole-row UpsertScreen carries it for free, so no new mutation kind is needed.

entries.description: The ordered source list (at least one entry).

items.description: The signal carried by a WorldScreen's lit face. A source declares which provider feeds a slot; the engine resolves and samples it. The $type string is the JSON discriminator; a new source kind is a new derived record plus its JsonDerivedTypeAttribute line.

anyOf.description: No provider is bound — the engine lights the slot with its procedural no-signal fallback (an animated test-card / striped no-signal look, never black).

background.description: The cell background color as #RRGGBB, or null for black.

selected.description: The 0-based entry the selector starts on (what screen.select advances from), not what the screen boots showing — a screen always wakes on its declared Source (the one-live-console ceiling depends on this). wrap.description: Whether advancing past the last entry returns to the first (the arcade cabinet's wrapping cycle); when false the selector clamps at both ends.

items.description: One placeable camera composed from a reference frame, local motion, framing policy, lens, and render target.

name.description: The camera's stable name — the handle a View screen / layout slot samples by.

anchor.description: What the camera rides, or null for the world reference frame.

anyOf.description: Rides one population entity's ROOT pose — a walking avatar's whole-body position and orientation.

index.description: The 0-based entity index, bounded by the world's authored population capacity.

anyOf.description: Rides one entity look's authored part pose rather than its whole-body root. The active look publishes the mapping from PartId to its packed transform slot; the slot remains an engine detail.

partId.description: The ordinal, case-sensitive part identifier published by the entity's active look.

anyOf.description: Rides a placement INSTANCE's stamped transform — a creation stamped into the world by reference (the same placement-reference shape CreationCameraDocument uses), optionally narrowed to one of its own authored shapes rather than the stamp's root.

shapeId.description: The referenced creation's ShapeDocument.Id to ride, or null for the placement's own stamped root transform.

anyOf.description: Rides the smoothed CENTROID of a set of population entities — the establishing-shot anchor. Also publishes the set's SPREAD (mean distance from the centroid), which a camera program's Offset consumes through its SpreadPullback. A group has no facing, so its orientation resolves to identity.

indices.description: The 0-based entity indices in the set, or null for the whole live population (every active entity). Each index is validated 0..127.

smoothRate.description: The exponential smoothing rate (per second) the centroid/spread ease at (validated positive and finite) — seeded un-smoothed on first resolve so a camera does not fly in from the origin.

rig.description: The independent local motion, aim, and lens axes.

name.description: The stable name a Blend op selects this program by.

operations.description: The selected ops, in authored evaluation order.

items.description: One instruction in an authored camera program's ordered op list — the presentation-side pose algebra bodyMotionPrograms established for sim-side movement, promoted to cameras: an authored rig is an ordered list of these trivial ops rather than a bespoke closed motion/aim union, so a new camera behavior is authored data, never new engine code. This is the AUTHORING vocabulary only: Puck.World.Client.WorldCameraRigCompiler translates it to Puck.SdfVm.Views.SdfCameraOp and resolves each frame's bindings and subject poses, and Puck.SdfVm.Views.SdfCameraProgramEvaluator — which parses no document — walks the result. Floats throughout; presentation carries no fixed-point burden.

anyOf.description: Establishes the CURRENT subject — the pose Offset/Orbit place the eye relative to, and LookAt aims along the facing of when it names no subject of its own. Also re-seeds the eye at the resolved subject's own position (the "first person" default before any Offset/Orbit runs). At most one per program, and it must be the first operation when present; a program that omits it starts from Reference implicitly.

The program's externally supplied reference pose — a named camera's own WorldAnchor, or a seat rig's currently perceived body (the seat's own avatar, or a possessed camera body). Resolved outside the program and handed to it as the SdfAnchor the compiled rig receives every frame.

Rides a placement's authored stamped transform (position only — a placement carries no live facing through this static resolve, the same limitation a placeable camera's own Placement arm and a speaker share).

shapeId.description: The referenced creation's own shape to ride, or null for the placement's stamped root transform.

anyOf.description: A fixed world-space point.

opcode.description: Gets this op's authored $type token — the one spelling a refusal, a read-back, and the document all use.

anyOf.description: Places the eye at an offset from the current subject's pose.

World (the default) takes the two channels as axes already in world frame — the seat's client composes the camera yaw into the submitted intent before it ever reaches the wire, so the sim never reads a camera pose (determinism: no camera state enters simulation).

Only the Face roles turn the heading itself. Ignored under Heading, where attitude is the integrated heading by construction. true is the default.

moveSpeedEnvelope.description: The inclusive bound a seated player's live profile speed (and the profileless MoveSpeed fallback) is clamped to at seat time, or null (the default) for no bound — a feel-pinned world authors this to keep a seat's speed inside its own kit's envelope regardless of what the player's identity requests. null reproduces today's unclamped behavior exactly; Min == Max pins the effective speed outright; a narrower-than-wide-open range still admits a bounded profile override. The one sprint-resolution read Compile and the seat binding surfaces share, so a new arm extends it here instead of each caller growing its own cast chain.

declaredMoveFrame.description: The declared move frame of whichever arm this is — Heading for an arm without the choice. The client's camera composition keys off this, arm-agnostically.

declaredTurnSpeed.description: The declared Turn-channel rate of whichever arm this is, in radians per second at full deflection — zero for an arm without one. The client's steer follow keys off this, arm-agnostically.

anyOf.description: Anisotropic body-frame locomotion — the racing-vehicle arm the ResolveVehicleFrame/ ShapeVehicleVelocity operations read. Velocity decomposes into longitudinal/lateral (and residual) body-frame components, each converging at its own authored rate — what separates a vehicle from Grounded, whose isotropic planar shaping cannot tune grip apart from acceleration. Steering authority scales with longitudinal speed (no spinning in place, looser at top speed) and reverses sign with reversing travel. One row serves the ground, hover, and air variants: a contact-pinned variant pairs this arm with a program keeping ApplyVerticalGravity (grounded-style vertical ownership and ramp ballistics), a flying variant pairs it with ApplyVerticalDecay and a positive PitchRate so climb emerges from the pitched facing.

topSpeed.description: The forward speed (u/s) full throttle converges on.

reverseTopSpeed.description: The reverse speed (u/s) full back-throttle converges on from rest; 0 forbids reversing.

accel.description: The longitudinal convergence rate (u/s²) while throttle commands more speed.

brake.description: The longitudinal convergence rate (u/s²) while back-throttle opposes forward travel.

coastDrag.description: The longitudinal convergence rate (u/s²) toward rest with throttle centered, and the decay rate while over the commanded speed (the post-boost bleed).

grip.description: The lateral convergence rate (u/s²) toward zero slip — traction. Lower is slidier.

steerRate.description: The yaw rate (rad/s) at full steering authority.

steerReferenceSpeed.description: The longitudinal speed (u/s) at which steering authority peaks; authority rises linearly from zero at standstill.

steerFalloff.description: The fraction of full steering authority remaining at TopSpeed, in [0, 1]; authority falls linearly from the reference speed.

pitchRate.description: The pitch rate (rad/s) the Pitch channel commands; 0 locks the frame planar (the ground and hover variants). Positive selects the flying variant's pitched facing, clamped inside the integrator so the frame can never flip past vertical.

riseGravity.description: The upward-motion gravity (u/s²) — the contact-pinned variant's arc top, and the flying variant's vertical-impulse bleed rate (via ApplyVerticalDecay).

maxFallSpeed.description: The terminal fall speed (u/s) under ApplyVerticalGravity.

driftGrip.description: The lateral convergence rate (u/s²) replacing Grip while DriftChannel reads held — the deliberate low-traction state. Required positive when a drift channel is declared; ignored without one.

driftSteerScale.description: The steering-authority multiplier while drifting (the tightened drift arc).

boostMultiplier.description: The TopSpeed multiplier while BoostChannel reads held; 1 is a no-op. The timed item boost is planarImpulse, not this.

driftChannel.description: The declared channel name read while held to drift, or null for a kit that cannot drift. Resolved to an ordinal once by Compile.

boostChannel.description: The declared channel name read while held to boost, or null for a kit with no held boost. Resolved through the same held-channel seam as SprintChannel.

topSpeedEnvelope.description: The racing-integrity clamp: the inclusive bound the resolved base TopSpeed is pinned to at resolve time — a live world.row.set kits retune (deliberately admitted even past the bound; WorldDefinitionValidator checks only the envelope's own shape, never that TopSpeed already sits inside it — the clamp exists precisely to catch a retune the envelope disagrees with, so requiring conformance up front would refuse the case it exists for), and any future per-seat vehicle stat resolve, both pass through it, or null (the default) for no bound. BoostMultiplier multiplies after this clamp, never before — the envelope pins the base top speed, boost rides on top, the same sprint-after-clamp precedent MoveSpeedEnvelope established for the grounded arm. The vehicle arm's resolve deliberately never reads a seated profile's speed (a kart's speed is the kit's), so this is the only seat-time clamp the vehicle arm has — unlike the grounded arm's envelope, which bounds a fallback a separate live profile read can diverge from, so grounded's own baseline is still required to sit inside its own bound. See MotionScalarEnvelope.

max.description: The greatest admitted value (inclusive) — WorldDefinitionValidator refuses Max < Min by name. Equal to Min pins the scalar outright regardless of what a profile requests.

declaredSprintChannel.description: The declared held-multiplier channel of whichever arm this is — SprintChannel, SprintChannel, or the vehicle arm's BoostChannel (the same held-multiplier seam under a different name) — or null for an arm (or a declaration) without one. The one sprint-resolution read Compile and the seat binding surfaces share, so a new arm extends it here instead of each caller growing its own cast chain.

declaredTurnSpeed.description: The declared Turn-channel rate of whichever arm this is, in radians per second at full deflection — zero for an arm without one. The client's steer follow keys off this, arm-agnostically.

anyOf.description: Submerged locomotion in the world's standing-water medium (the water section, which a kit declaring this arm requires): 3D thrust in the body's yaw frame with an explicit vertical channel, planar velocity converged through the response table (thrust against water drag — the engage rate is thrust authority, the release rate is the drag coast), and a single vertical channel owned end to end by the surface stage — the medium's own drift/settle folded into the commanded thrust target before that same response-row convergence runs, so nothing else writes vertical velocity independently. The ops family: ResolveYawAttitudeAndPlanarFrame, ComputeSwimTargetVelocity, ShapePlanarVelocity, ApplyBuoyancyAndSurface, IntegratePlanarAndVerticalVelocity. The body's attitude stays a pure yaw rotation. Aim-directed diving is the seat's composition, and only under World (MoveFrame): the rendered camera's elevation splits the commanded forward direction into planar and vertical channels client-side (the same determinism seam MoveFrame documents), never a camera pose entering the sim. The explicit MoveUp channel this splits into is orthogonal to that composition and stays live regardless of MoveFrame — a body dives on raw MoveUp input alone with no aim-composed seat at all.

thrustSpeed.description: Peak swim speed in world units per second — the profileless fallback (a seated player reads its live profile's move speed instead, exactly as MoveSpeed does).

turnSpeed.description: Turn speed in radians per second (the profileless fallback counterpart).

verticalThrustFraction.description: The fraction of ThrustSpeed the vertical channel commands — swimmers climb and dive slower than they cruise. 1 is fully isotropic thrust.

response.description: The velocity-response table (see MotionResponse) — it affects the simulation, read for both the planar and the vertical convergence. The empty table snaps instantly (no drag, no coast); a water feel wants at least an always-row.

buoyancy.description: The medium's idle vertical drift velocity (u/s, signed) below the bob band: positive drifts the body up toward its float line, negative sinks, zero holds depth. Folded into the commanded thrust target — see FixedSwimTuning — never applied as a separate acceleration.

maxRiseSpeed.description: The terminal ascent speed (u/s) the vertical channel is clamped to.

maxSinkSpeed.description: The terminal descent speed (u/s) the vertical channel is clamped to.

surfaceSettleRate.description: The proportional settle gain (1/s) toward the float line, applied inside the bob band and above it (breach recovery): the medium's target velocity there is the displacement from the line times this gain, so a held ascent parks where thrust and settle balance instead of breaching.

floatDepth.description: How far below the waterline (world units) the body origin rests when floating — and the bob band's half-width around that rest line (one knob deliberately: the band a body settles in is the depth scale it settles at). The validator only checks this is positive and finite — it cannot see the document's contact geometry, so it does not (and cannot) check this against the local water column's depth. A FloatDepth deeper than the floor below it parks the body on the floor instead of at the float line, with AtSurface never true there — a geometry fact deliberately outside this validator's reach.

sprintMultiplier.description: The held-burst speed multiplier applied while SprintChannel reads held; 1 is a no-op. Scales the whole thrust vector, vertical included.

sprintChannel.description: The declared channel name read while held for the burst, or null (the default) for a kit with no burst — the same resolution path SprintChannel documents.

moveFrame.description: Which frame MoveAdvance/MoveStrafe resolve in — the same two-frame choice, and the same client-side camera composition seam, as MoveFrame.

facingSnap.description: Under World only: snap facing to the commanded planar direction each tick carrying input, as FacingSnap documents.

thrustSpeedEnvelope.description: The inclusive bound a seated player's live profile speed (and the profileless ThrustSpeed fallback) is clamped to at seat time, or null (the default) for no bound — the same seam as MoveSpeedEnvelope, for this arm's own thrust speed. null reproduces unclamped behavior exactly; Min == Max pins the effective thrust speed outright regardless of what a profile requests. See MotionScalarEnvelope.

max.description: The greatest admitted value (inclusive) — WorldDefinitionValidator refuses Max < Min by name. Equal to Min pins the scalar outright regardless of what a profile requests.

declaredSprintChannel.description: The declared held-multiplier channel of whichever arm this is — SprintChannel, SprintChannel, or the vehicle arm's BoostChannel (the same held-multiplier seam under a different name) — or null for an arm (or a declaration) without one. The one sprint-resolution read Compile and the seat binding surfaces share, so a new arm extends it here instead of each caller growing its own cast chain.

declaredMoveFrame.description: The declared move frame of whichever arm this is — Heading for an arm without the choice. The client's camera composition keys off this, arm-agnostically.

declaredTurnSpeed.description: The declared Turn-channel rate of whichever arm this is, in radians per second at full deflection — zero for an arm without one. The client's steer follow keys off this, arm-agnostically.

collider.description: The kit's collider, when it authors one.

anyOf.description: A sphere resting on the body root.
A capsule whose lower sphere rests on the body root.

endpoint.description: The body-local vector from the lower sphere center to the upper sphere center.

anyOf.description: An oriented box resting on the body root before its local rotation is applied.
The finite primitive bounds emitted by a creation, composed into one compound body collider.

bodyContact.description: Whether two bodies wearing this kit physically depenetrate.

sequence.description: The sequence that selects a row.

name.description: The sequence name: None, Index, Additive, R1, or R2.

offset.description: The signed phase added to the caller's stable index before sampling.

step.description: The turn-sized increment for Additive; zero for every other sequence.

rows.description: Gets the authored row-name view. The absence-coalesce lives in the accessor for the same reason Response's does.

bindingOverlays.description: The world's binding layers — a visitor's seat composes over them.

items.description: One per-world binding overlay — a whole BindingProfileDocument layered over the engine default beneath every seat's profile bindings, so a world can contextualize the controls (a kart world remapping a lane, an RTS world adding a chorded command page) as data, never a client fork. Merged in order; the composed result (default ⊕ every overlay) is what the validator compiles.

id.description: The overlay's stable id — its mutation address (unique within the definition; carries no meaning beyond identity).

document.description: The overlay binding document merged into the composed mapping.

bindingBar.description: The on-screen bar policy carried with this binding layer; null carries no policy on this layer, so bar resolution falls through to the world-authored policy, and to Absent (no bar drawn) when neither an identity nor the world authors one.

slotSet.description: The physical buttons this bar shows, in authored order (an exotic button's left-to-right position in its row follows this order) — every name validated against the full GamepadButtons catalog by name, unique, so the catalog itself bounds the count (the reservation sizes from Puck.Input.Devices.GamepadButtonCatalog.Count).

banks.description: The stacked banks — at least one, at most MaxBanks, unique ids, each naming a page the composed binding profile actually declares.

items.description: One stacked binding-bar bank: the page it renders and where it renders relative to the bar's shared anchor. Several banks of the SAME slot set render simultaneously, each showing what that bank's OWN page binds — the WoW-addon original's "five banks of one compass" idea (resting, LT, RT, LT>RT, RT>LT are the natural five, though a bank may name any page).

id.description: The bank's stable id — its mutation address (unique within the authoring row).

pageId.description: The BindingPageDefinition.Id this bank renders — validated to exist somewhere in the composed binding profile.

offsetX.description: This bank's horizontal displacement from the bar's shared anchor, in region-height units (the same unit WorldBindingBarLayout's lengths use).

offsetY.description: This bank's vertical displacement, region-height units, Y DOWN (positive moves toward the bottom of the seat's viewport).

alpha.description: This bank's opacity when it is NOT the seat's currently active page.

activeAlpha.description: This bank's opacity when it IS the seat's currently active page; null draws fully opaque (1.0) while active.

enabled.description: Whether the bar is shown when no live override hides it.

text.description: Whether the bar draws the ATLAS TEXT it composes — a badge whose icon row carries a Label (LB/RB, LT/RT, LS/RS, the menu trio, the exotics), the active page's name under the modifier indicators, and the chord-hint lines above them. false drops every label-content badge outright and leaves a purely pictographic bar: every plate, the glyph-content badges (the d-pad arrows and the face-position marks), the bound actions' icons, and the modifier indicators all still draw.

hideUnbound.description: Whether a slot with no bound act on its bank's page should not render at all, rather than drawing the DISABLED tier-0 plate. A player's own BindingBarPreferences.HideUnbound overrides this.

multiSeatAlpha.description: The opacity every joined seat's bar renders at while two or more seats are joined — the split-screen quieting lever, multiplied into each bank's own alpha; 1 keeps multi-seat bars fully opaque.

layout.description: The bar's tuning; null uses Default.

centerGap.description: The unscaled extra half-gap between the mirrored clusters.

anchorOffsetY.description: The anchor's lift above the viewport's bottom edge.

glyphOffsetRatio.description: The gamepad glyph's corner offset as a fraction of ButtonSize.

glyphSizeRatio.description: The gamepad glyph's size as a fraction of ButtonSize.

visible.description: The bar's visibility condition over presentation facts, or null for always.

anyOf.description: The fact holds this frame.
The fact held within the last WindowSeconds.

items.description: An overlay element's visibility condition — the presentation twin of ActionPredicate, over OverlayFacts. Absent on an element means always visible.
